# DSP Architecture: O-Tapestop

**CRITICAL CONTRACT:** This specification is immutable during Stages 1-4 implementation. Stage 1 Planning cannot proceed without this file. Stage 2 (DSP) implements this exact architecture.

**Generated by:** Stage 0 Research (research-planning-agent, 2026-08-15)
**Referenced by:** Stage 1 (Foundation), Stage 2 (DSP Implementation), Stage 3 (GUI)
**Complexity tier:** 3 (complex DSP algorithms — varispeed engine, resync, drawn-envelope modulation)
**Research depth:** MODERATE

---

## Core Components

### Capture Ring (CaptureBuffer)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom — reuse `plugins/O-ReverseDelay/Source/dsp/CaptureBuffer.h` verbatim (absolute-index stereo ring, `int64 totalWritten`, double-mod `readAbs`, alloc-free `clear()`)
- **Purpose:** Continuous recording of the live input; all wet playback reads from this ring
- **Parameters Affected:** none directly (sized by constants)
- **Configuration:**
  - `kCaptureSeconds = 26.0f` — derivation below (Ring Sizing)
  - Freeze machinery (`pushLooped`/`pushCrossfaded`) unused in v1.0 — plain `pushSample` only
  - Written **every sample, every block, in every state** (including Bypassed) so engage always has history
  - Per-sample ordering inside the render loop: **write capture first, then read** (memory pattern: grain read latched before the block's capture write breaks at blockSize ≥ D; per-sample write-then-read makes 512-vs-4096 bit-identity structural)

### Varispeed Voice Engine (VarispeedVoice + VoiceXfade)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom — adapted from `ReverseGrain.h` (direction/step concept, latch-at-spawn contract) + `WindowLut.h` (Hann table for equal-power crossfade ramps). `GrainScheduler.h` is **not** used (no periodic spawning; voice spawns are event-driven, max 2 concurrent).
- **Purpose:** Single fractional-position playhead over the capture ring with per-sample speed `r` (bipolar). A second voice exists only during crossfade transitions (resync skip, scratch retrigger, abort-to-live).
- **Parameters Affected:** ENGAGE, MODE (selects who drives `r`)
- **Configuration:**
  - Read position: `double readAbsFrac` against `CaptureBuffer::totalWritten`; per-sample `readAbsFrac += r`
  - Interpolation: 4-point Catmull-Rom on `readAbs(ch, i-1..i+2)` (fractional varispeed needs interpolation; O-ReverseDelay dropped it only because its speed was exactly ±1)
  - **Stereo:** voice reads both channels via `readAbs(0/1, …)` (no monoSum — this is full-signal varispeed, the stereo image must survive)
  - **Debt** `d = totalWritten − readAbsFrac`, clamped to `[kInterpGuard=4, ringSpan − kInterpGuard]`; if the envelope demands `r > 1` at `d ≈ 0`, the voice rides the live head (pass-through) — read never crosses the write head
  - When `d` is exactly the integer 0-offset and `r == 1` (Bypassed/live-riding), read the **integer** index — output is bitwise dry (enables DSP-03 null)
  - Crossfades: two-voice overlap, gains from the WindowLut Hann half (`fadeOut = hann(0.5 + φ/2)`, `fadeIn = hann(φ/2)`, equal-power); duration `kSkipXfadeMs = 50 ms`

### Transport State Machine + Ramp Generator
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (`TapestopTransport`)
- **Purpose:** Drives `r(t)` per sample from the engage lifecycle; owns the curve-morph law
- **Parameters Affected:** ENGAGE, MODE, STOP_SYNC_DIV/STOP_FREE_MS, START_SYNC_DIV/START_FREE_MS, SYNC_MODE, STOP_CURVE, START_CURVE
- **Configuration:**
  - States: `Bypassed → SpinDown → Stopped → SpinUp → Catchup → ResyncXfade → Bypassed` (Stop mode); `Bypassed → ScratchPass → ResyncXfade → Bypassed` (Scratch mode)
  - Curve morph: `r(u) = (1−u)^p` (spin-down), `r(u) = u^p` (spin-up), with `p = 2^(2c)` for curve c ∈ [0,1]: c=0 → p=1 (linear), c=0.5 → p=2 (**exactly x², the tape-physics default — DSP-02 by construction**), c=1 → p=4 (exponential-feel). Monotonic, continuous, exact at the contract point.
  - Ramp durations latched **in samples at the triggering edge** (tempo converted once per gesture; a mid-ramp tempo change does not retarget a live ramp — latch-at-spawn contract)
  - **Mid-ramp reversal (FUNC-01):** on an engage edge mid-ramp, the new ramp resumes speed-continuously: `u0 = r0^(1/p_new)` (inverse of the new curve at the current ratio). Speed is continuous ⇒ position is C¹ ⇒ no click.
  - **Stopped (FUNC-04):** entered when `r < kStopEps (0.001)`; a 10 ms linear output-gain fade to exact silence (a frozen playhead otherwise holds a DC sample). Exit on disengage.

### Resync Controller (DSP-03)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (part of `TapestopTransport`)
- **Purpose:** Signalsmith fall-behind → accelerate → crossfade-skip (KVR t=538470)
- **Parameters Affected:** START_CURVE, START_SYNC_DIV/START_FREE_MS
- **Configuration:**
  - **Fall-behind:** SpinUp ramps `r` 0→1 per startCurve over startTime; playhead intentionally lags real time (debt grows by `∫(1−r)dt` — for x² over 8 s, up to ~5.3 s)
  - **Accelerate:** `Catchup` state holds `r = kCatchupRatio = 1.25` for at most `kMaxCatchupMs = 250 ms` (musical overspeed garnish; shaves debt and telegraphs the rejoin)
  - **Crossfade-skip:** spawn voice B at the live head (`d = 0`, `r = 1`, integer-offset read); 50 ms equal-power Hann crossfade A→B; discard A; → Bypassed
  - Post-crossfade output = integer-offset live read = **bitwise dry** ⇒ null test passes by construction
  - Alternative documented in Risks: repeated small skips (granular time-compress) if the single skip is judged too abrupt on sustained material

### Scratch Envelope System (FUNC-02, DSP-04)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (`ScratchEnvelope` bake + playback); persistence via `juce::ValueTree` property (JSON string) inside APVTS state
- **Purpose:** User-drawn bipolar speed-vs-time curve, played once per engage in Scratch mode
- **Parameters Affected:** MODE, ENV_SYNC_DIV/ENV_FREE_MS, ENGAGE
- **Configuration:**
  - **Point model:** `{x ∈ [0,1], y ∈ [−1,1], curve ∈ [−1,1]}` sorted list, 2–64 points, first/last pinned at x=0/1 (Path C §2.1 model, y made bipolar)
  - **Speed map:** `r = 2·y` ⇒ r ∈ [−2, +2]; y = +0.5 is 1× (draw a labelled grid line there); y < 0 is reverse (voice `step` sign flips — position stays continuous, so a flip is a palindrome corner, not a click)
  - **Audio-thread handoff:** message thread bakes the point list into a fixed 2048-float speed LUT in one of two pre-allocated buffers; publishes via `std::atomic<ScratchLut*>` pointer swap. Audio thread **latches the LUT pointer at the engage edge** — edits mid-pass affect the next pass only (same latch-at-spawn contract as everything else). Zero allocation, zero locks on the audio thread.
  - **Playback:** pass phase `φ = samplesElapsed / envLengthSamples` (envLength latched at edge); `r = lut[φ·2047]` with linear interp; at φ = 1 → ResyncXfade to live. Disengage mid-pass → abort straight to ResyncXfade.
  - **Persistence:** JSON `{"points":[{"x":…,"y":…,"curve":…},…]}` stored as a string property on the APVTS state tree in `getStateInformation` (envelope is NOT an APVTS parameter — not automatable in v1.0)
  - **Default:** gentle wobble — `[{0, 0.5}, {0.25, 0.65}, {0.5, 0.35}, {0.75, 0.6}, {1, 0.5}]` (speed oscillating around 1×)

### Tempo Sync (FUNC-03)
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::AudioPlayHead::getPosition()` → `PositionInfo::getBpm()/getPpqPosition()` (JUCE 8 API, verified in local 8.0.14 tree)
- **Purpose:** Convert sync divisions (1/16 … 4 bars) to sample counts for stop/start/env times
- **Parameters Affected:** SYNC_MODE, STOP_SYNC_DIV, START_SYNC_DIV, ENV_SYNC_DIV
- **Configuration:**
  - Division table: {1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1 bar, 2 bars, 4 bars} → beats {0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16}
  - `durationSamples = beats · (60/bpm) · fs`, BPM read per block with the O-Polystutter fallback+clamp pattern (`PluginProcessor.cpp:1710–1719`): missing playhead/offline → 120 BPM fallback, clamp 20–999
  - Durations are latched at the gesture edge (see Transport) — this is what makes free-mode times "match wall-clock within one block" and keeps renders block-size invariant

### toneTrack Filter (DSP-05)
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::FirstOrderTPTFilter<float>` (lowpass mode) — verified in local JUCE 8.0.14 (`juce_dsp/processors/juce_FirstOrderTPTFilter.h:62`, `setCutoffFrequency:80`); TPT structure is modulation-safe; in-repo precedent: O-Bells, O-Formant
- **Purpose:** Physically-motivated darkening as speed drops (slower tape = duller)
- **Parameters Affected:** TONE_TRACK
- **Configuration:**
  - Cutoff law (log map): `fc = fMax · (fMin/fMax)^(a · (1 − min(|r|,1)))` with fMax = 20 kHz, fMin = 150 Hz, a = TONE_TRACK/100
  - a = 0 ⇒ fc = fMax always (effectively off, no conditional path — no click when sweeping the knob through 0)
  - Cutoff updated every **16-sample sub-block** (control rate; `setCutoffFrequency` computes a tan — not per-sample). A 16-sample update grid is fs-independent in samples, keeping block-size invariance (update boundaries at absolute sample positions, not block starts).
  - Wet-path only, engaged-only; **state reset at the engage edge** (starts wide-open, one-pole from zero state converges in <1 ms — inaudible), so the Bypassed path stays untouched bitwise dry
  - RT-safe: TPT coefficient update is a closed-form per-call computation, no allocation (satisfies the ArrayCoefficients-class concern for this topology)

### Mix + Output Gain
- **JUCE Class:** Custom linear blend + `juce::SmoothedValue<float>` for gain
- **Purpose:** Dry/wet blend and output trim
- **Parameters Affected:** MIX, OUTPUT_GAIN
- **Configuration:**
  - Bypassed state: `output = input` directly (skip the blend arithmetic entirely — bitwise null regardless of MIX)
  - Engaged: `out = dry·(1−m) + wet·m` per sample, m smoothed (20 ms)
  - OUTPUT_GAIN dB → linear via SmoothedValue (20 ms), applied last
  - No `juce::dsp::DryWetMixer` (its latency-compensation machinery is unneeded at zero latency, and it would break the bitwise-bypass guarantee)

## Processing Chain

```
Input (stereo)
  │
  ├──────────────────────────────► dry copy (per-block, pre-allocated scratch)
  │
  ▼  (per sample: WRITE first)
CaptureBuffer (26 s absolute-index ring, always written)
  │
  ▼  (per sample: READ second)
VarispeedVoice A [+ Voice B during crossfades]
  ▲ r(t) per sample from ───┐
  │                         │
  │   TapestopTransport (state machine)
  │     ├─ Stop mode:   curve ramps ← STOP_*/START_*/SYNC_MODE, curves
  │     ├─ Scratch mode: ScratchLut[φ] ← ENV_*, drawn envelope (latched at edge)
  │     └─ Resync: fall-behind → 1.25× catchup → 50 ms crossfade-skip
  │
  ▼
toneTrack LPF (FirstOrderTPT, fc ← |r| + TONE_TRACK, engaged-only)
  │
  ▼
Stopped-state silence fade (10 ms, only entering/leaving r≈0)
  │
  ▼
Dry/Wet blend ← MIX          (Bypassed state: output = input, bitwise)
  │
  ▼
Output gain ← OUTPUT_GAIN (smoothed)
  │
  ▼
Output
```

**Routing notes:**
- No feedback loops anywhere (unlike O-ReverseDelay — no loop tap, no dual window normalisation problem)
- Voice B path exists only during ResyncXfade / scratch retrigger; both voices pass through the same toneTrack filter (filter follows the *blended* ratio? No — filter cutoff follows **voice A's r until the crossfade midpoint, then voice B's** — in practice B's r is always 1.0 during resync, so cutoff simply continues its glide open; document as: cutoff driven by the dominant voice's ratio)
- Latency: 0 samples (causal effect; the wet path lags *content*, not the I/O stream). No `setLatencySamples` needed.

## System Architecture

### State Persistence
**What state is saved:**
- APVTS parameters (14) — automatic
- `scratchEnvelope` point list — JSON string property on the APVTS state tree (NOT a parameter)

**Serialization format:** APVTS ValueTree → XML (automatic); envelope JSON embedded as one string property `scratchEnvelopeJson`.

**JUCE classes:** `AudioProcessorValueTreeState`, `juce::ValueTree`, `juce::JSON` (parse/format), `juce::MemoryBlock`.

**Restore behavior:**
- Missing/invalid envelope JSON → default gentle-wobble envelope, no error
- Malformed points (unsorted x, out-of-range y) → sanitize on parse (clamp, sort, pin endpoints)
- Version field `"v":1` in the JSON for future migration (memory pattern: per-param version gates; give the blob its own version from day one)

### File I/O — none. Multi-output routing — none (stereo in/out only). MIDI — none in v1.0 (deferred per REQUIREMENTS Out-of-Scope).

## Parameter Mapping

| Parameter ID | Type | Range | DSP Component | Usage |
|-------------|------|-------|---------------|-------|
| ENGAGE | Bool | Off/On | Transport | Edge-triggered lifecycle (detect per block); On=spin-down/scratch-pass, Off=spin-up+resync |
| MODE | Choice | Stop/Scratch | Transport | Selects ramp source; switching while disengaged is silent (Bypassed path untouched) |
| SYNC_MODE | Choice | Sync/Free | Tempo Sync | Selects division vs ms source for all three times |
| STOP_SYNC_DIV | Choice | 1/16…4 bars | Transport | Spin-down duration (Sync), latched at edge |
| STOP_FREE_MS | Float | 10–8000 ms, skew 0.35 | Transport | Spin-down duration (Free), default 500 |
| STOP_CURVE | Float | 0–100 % | Ramp Generator | p = 2^(2c); 50 % = x² exactly |
| START_SYNC_DIV | Choice | 1/16…4 bars | Transport | Spin-up duration (Sync), default 1/4 bar |
| START_FREE_MS | Float | 10–8000 ms, skew 0.35 | Transport | Spin-up duration (Free), default 250 |
| START_CURVE | Float | 0–100 % | Ramp Generator | Same law as STOP_CURVE |
| ENV_SYNC_DIV | Choice | 1/16…4 bars | Scratch Envelope | One pass duration (Sync), default 1 bar |
| ENV_FREE_MS | Float | 10–8000 ms, skew 0.35 | Scratch Envelope | Pass duration (Free), default 1000 |
| TONE_TRACK | Float | 0–100 % | toneTrack Filter | Depth of speed→cutoff tracking; 0 = fc pinned at 20 kHz |
| MIX | Float | 0–100 % | Mix | Wet proportion; Bypassed state ignores it (bitwise dry) |
| OUTPUT_GAIN | Float | −24…+12 dB | Output Gain | Smoothed dB trim |

Non-APVTS state: `scratchEnvelopeJson` (drawn curve blob, see Scratch Envelope System).

## Algorithm Details

### Varispeed Read (DSP-01)

**Algorithm:** Fractional-position playhead over the absolute-index ring; Catmull-Rom 4-point interpolation.

**Implementation notes:**
- `sample = catmullRom(ring[⌊p⌋−1 … ⌊p⌋+2], frac(p))` per channel; `p += r` per sample
- A continuous position under any bounded speed law is click-free by construction — clicks only occur at position *jumps*, and every jump in this design is a 50 ms two-voice equal-power crossfade
- Direction flips (scratch): `r` crosses 0 ⇒ position corner (palindrome). Authentic turntable behaviour, not an artifact.
- **Why not overlap-add grains for steady playback:** periodic forward grains at near-unit rate all read coherent material and sum in *amplitude* while the 1/√overlap gain assumes *power* summing (memory pattern: forward-grain coherent sum) — level error, comb risk, and the engine could never produce a bitwise-dry output for the DSP-03 null test. The grain substrate's value here is the ring, the window LUT, and the latch-at-spawn discipline — not the periodic scheduler.

### Curve Morph (DSP-02)

**Algorithm:** `r(u) = (1−u)^p` (down), `u^p` (up), `p = 2^(2c)`, c = curve/100.

**Implementation notes:**
- c = 0.5 ⇒ p = 2 ⇒ x² exactly (turntable physics: constant friction torque ⇒ linear angular-velocity decay ⇒ x² feels right because pitch falls as r — verified against Kilohearts Tape Stop's Curve control concept)
- Evaluate per sample: `u += 1/durationSamples`, one `pow` per sample is fine (or evaluate `pow` every 16 samples and linearly interpolate — decide at implementation; per-sample pow of a slowly-varying base is ~15 ns, acceptable at ≤2 voices)
- Reversal continuity: `u0 = clamp(r0, 0, 1)^(1/p_new)` seeds the new ramp

### Resync (DSP-03)

**Algorithm:** Three-phase (Signalsmith, KVR t=538470): ramp (fall-behind) → constant 1.25× (accelerate, ≤250 ms) → single 50 ms equal-power crossfade-skip to the live head.

**Implementation notes:**
- Skip lands on integer offset 0 at `r = 1` ⇒ post-crossfade samples are the ring's copy of the current input, read at integer indices ⇒ **null vs dry is exact** (given per-sample write-then-read order)
- The null-test window in the render harness starts one full crossfade after Catchup ends
- Debt after an 8 s x² spin-up ≈ 5.3 s — the skip is *supposed* to jump that content; it is the DJ-releases-the-record gesture

### Scratch Envelope Bake

**Algorithm:** Piecewise curve interpolation (Path C §2.1 `getValueAt` with per-segment `pow` curve) evaluated at 2048 uniform φ points on the message thread; audio thread reads the LUT with linear interpolation.

**Implementation notes:**
- Bake on: state restore, editor edit commit (mouse-up + 50 ms debounce), preset load
- Double-buffer + atomic pointer publish; audio thread never parses JSON or walks the point list
- LUT resolution: 2048 points over ≥10 ms ⇒ worst-case segment resolution 5 µs — far beyond audibility for a speed control

### toneTrack Cutoff Law

**Algorithm:** `fc = 20000 · (150/20000)^(a·(1−min(|r|,1)))`, a = amount.

**Implementation notes:**
- At r = 0, a = 1: fc = 150 Hz (deep muffle at full stop); at r = 1 or a = 0: fc = 20 kHz
- |r| > 1 (catchup/scratch overspeed) clamps to open — overspeed should not *brighten* beyond flat
- One `pow` + one `setCutoffFrequency` per 16-sample sub-block

## Integration Points

### Feature Dependencies
- Capture ring → Varispeed voice: all wet reads come from the ring; ring must be written before any read of the same sample index (per-sample write-then-read)
- Transport → Voice: transport owns `r(t)`; voice only integrates it
- Tempo sync → Transport: durations converted at gesture edges only (latch contract)
- Scratch envelope bake (message thread) → Transport (audio thread): atomic LUT pointer, latched at engage edge
- Resync → Voice crossfade: resync spawns voice B and drives the crossfade gains
- toneTrack ← Transport's current `r`: filter cutoff is a *consumer* of the ratio, never an influence on it
- Envelope editor (UI) → Envelope bake: WebView native functions commit point lists; UI is never on the audio path

### Parameter Interactions
- SYNC_MODE gates which of each SYNC_DIV/FREE_MS pair is read — both params always exist; only the edge-latch reads them (mid-gesture flips are inert)
- MODE gates STOP_*/START_* (Stop) vs ENV_* (Scratch); disengaged mode switches are silent because the Bypassed path touches nothing (FUNC-02 acceptance)
- STOP_CURVE/START_CURVE interact with mid-ramp reversal: the inverse-curve seed uses the *new* direction's curve
- TONE_TRACK at 0 must be sonically transparent but need not be bitwise (wet path is already non-dry while engaged); Bypassed bitwise-null is guaranteed by routing, not by filter settings
- MIX < 100 % during Stopped state: dry keeps playing under silence-faded wet — correct parallel behaviour, no special case

### Processing Order Requirements
1. Read APVTS atomics, detect ENGAGE edge, update transport state (per block header)
2. Per sample: write input to capture ring
3. Per sample: advance transport (`r`, state transitions, crossfade phase)
4. Per sample: voice read(s) + crossfade blend → wet
5. Per 16-sample boundary: update toneTrack cutoff from current `r`
6. Per sample: filter wet, apply stopped-fade, blend with dry, output gain
7. Bypassed fast path: steps 3–6 replaced by `out = in` (ring still written in step 2)

### Thread Boundaries
- **Audio thread:** everything in the chain above; APVTS atomic reads; atomic LUT pointer load; zero allocation/locks (PERF-01)
- **Message thread:** envelope JSON parse/serialize, LUT bake + atomic publish, WebView native fns, state save/restore
- **No background thread** (no file I/O)
- Communication: APVTS atomics; `std::atomic<ScratchLut*>` (double-buffered, message thread writes the inactive buffer only); engage-edge latch means the audio thread never reads a half-baked LUT mid-pass
- UI playhead/state readback (envelope pass position, current state) via `std::atomic<float>` + editor timer + `emitEventIfBrowserIsVisible` (O-Polystutter progress-bridge pattern; memory: WebView completions are dropped when hidden — gate emission on visibility)

## Implementation Risks

### Varispeed Voice Engine
**Complexity:** MEDIUM  **Risk Level:** LOW
- Risk factors: interpolation quality at extreme slow speeds (r < 0.05 exposes interpolation error as audible stair-stepping); read/write collision at r > 1
- Alternatives: Lagrange 4-point (Path C reference) vs Catmull-Rom — near-identical cost, either acceptable; upgrade to 6-point if slow-speed quality disappoints
- Fallback: none needed — this is the well-trodden core of every tapestop
- Mitigation: render-harness sine-sweep probe at r = 0.02; debt clamp asserted in debug

### Resync Controller
**Complexity:** MEDIUM  **Risk Level:** MEDIUM
- Risk factors: the single crossfade-skip jumps up to ~5 s of content — on sustained pads the splice could read as a hard edit; crossfading two *different* positions of correlated material can produce a level bump under equal-power law
- Alternatives: (1) repeated small crossfade-skips (~60 ms each) during Catchup — granular time-compress, smoother but busier; (2) linear (amplitude) crossfade instead of equal-power for the skip — correct for highly-correlated material
- Fallback: ship the single skip; if verification flags the splice, switch to repeated small skips (state machine already has the Catchup phase to hang them on)
- Mitigation: A/B linear-vs-equal-power on the skip during Phase 2.2; null-test probe defines done

### Scratch Envelope System (bake + handoff + bipolar playback)
**Complexity:** MEDIUM  **Risk Level:** MEDIUM
- Risk factors: ring debt under sustained reverse (bounded by design, but the clamp must degrade gracefully — a clamped read at the guard rail sounds like a loop point); envelope edits racing an active pass (solved by edge-latch); staircase-style drawn shapes create near-instant speed swings (legal — position stays continuous)
- Alternatives: audio-thread piecewise evaluation of the point list (rejected: variable-cost walk + curve `pow` per sample on the audio thread; the LUT is strictly better)
- Fallback: if the debt clamp is audible on abusive envelopes, soft-limit the *effective* r near the rail (scale r toward 0 within the last 250 ms of ring headroom)
- Mitigation: harness probe with worst-case full-reverse envelope at max envLength; assert debt < ring span

### Ring Sizing (memory-pattern static guard)
**Complexity:** LOW  **Risk Level:** LOW
- **Derivation (the contract):** worst case is Scratch, full-reverse: `d(debt)/dt = 1 − r`, r = −2 ⇒ 3 s of debt per second, over envLength_max = 8 s ⇒ 24 s. Stop mode bound: spin-down 8 s (≤ 8 s debt) + re-engage cycles ≤ stop+start ≈ 16 s. `kCaptureSeconds = 26.0` = 24 + 2 margin.
- Guard: `static_assert`-style constant derivation comment + runtime `jassert(debt <= ringSpan - guard)`; debt clamp as the release-build behaviour
- Memory cost: 26 s stereo float = 9.2 MB @ 44.1 kHz, 40 MB @ 192 kHz — acceptable, note in docs

### toneTrack Filter
**Complexity:** LOW  **Risk Level:** LOW
- Risk factors: none material; TPT one-pole is modulation-safe; NaN-guard hygiene per suite pattern (keep last-known-good behaviour is moot for TPT closed-form updates)
- Mitigation: pathological-input probe (silence/DC/full-scale impulse) with sticky-state checks (QUAL-01)

### Block-Size Invariance (QUAL-01)
**Complexity:** MEDIUM  **Risk Level:** MEDIUM
- Risk factors: this is where suite plugins historically failed (memory patterns: per-block envelope followers, block-latched reads, RNG interleave). O-Tapestop has **no RNG** and no envelope follower; the exposure is (a) ENGAGE edge detection granularity and (b) the 16-sample cutoff update grid.
- Design answers: (a) edges are detected per block — a 512-block and a 4096-block host *see the same automation timeline* only if the harness drives ENGAGE via `setParameter` at identical sample positions; the harness must schedule edges on block boundaries common to both sizes (multiples of 4096). (b) cutoff updates anchor to absolute sample count (`totalWritten % 16 == 0`), not block starts.
- Mitigation: 512-vs-4096 bit-identity probe is the Phase-2.1 gate, run from day one

### Overall Project Risk
**Overall complexity:** MEDIUM — one genuinely custom subsystem (transport/resync state machine); everything else is proven substrate or closed-form math.
**Highest risk component:** Resync controller (~50 % of risk) — the splice aesthetics, not the correctness, are the open question; correctness (null test) is guaranteed by construction.
**Recommended approach:** Build the voice + stop/start core first (validates the click-free claim and the null path), resync second, scratch + toneTrack last. Harness probes gate each phase.

---

## Architecture Decisions

### Single interpolated playhead + event-driven crossfade voices (not periodic overlap-add grains)
**Decision:** The wet path is ONE fractional-position voice; the grain machinery contributes the ring, WindowLut crossfades, the direction/latch-at-spawn contracts, and a max-2-voice pool — the periodic GrainScheduler is not used.
**Rationale:** (1) A continuous playhead under a bounded speed law cannot click — the brief's core promise is met structurally, not statistically. (2) Periodic forward grains at near-unit speed read coherent material and sum in amplitude against a power-law gain (documented suite memory pattern) — level errors and comb coloration on the *clean* portions of ramps. (3) DSP-03 demands a bitwise-dry null post-resync; an overlap-add engine can never produce bitwise dry. (4) The reuse-audit itself models tapestop as "varispeed read loop with ratio ramping" (RepeatLane `:183–217`).
**Alternatives considered:** Full grain overlap-add (rejected per above; reconsider *only* for the scratch pass if aggressive envelopes expose interpolation artifacts — 25–50 ms Hann micro-grains at latched speed, the O-ReverseDelay shape); naked linear-interp buffer reads without windowed crossfades (rejected: the skip/retrigger points would click — this is precisely what the brief warns against).
**Tradeoffs accepted:** Slightly more custom state-machine code vs. reusing GrainScheduler; accepted because the state machine is the product.

### Bypassed state = hard pass-through
**Decision:** Disengaged, the plugin outputs the input bitwise (no blend, no filter, ring still recording).
**Rationale:** FUNC-02 (mode switch silent while disengaged), DSP-03 (null), QUAL-01, and the resync contract all collapse to trivial once Bypassed is exact.
**Tradeoff:** MIX has no effect while disengaged — correct: there is no wet signal to mix.

### Envelope as state blob, not parameters
**Decision:** scratchEnvelope persists as one JSON string property; not automatable.
**Rationale:** Variable point count fits no fixed parameter set; suite precedent for state blobs; automation of the *shape* is out of scope (ENGAGE is the performance control).
**Alternatives:** N fixed point-parameters (rejected: 64 points × 3 fields of dead params); reconsider in v1.1 if envelope morph automation is requested.

### Speed range r ∈ [−2, +2] (envelope y ∈ [−1, 1], r = 2y)
**Decision:** Scratch speed spans double-speed both directions.
**Rationale:** ±1 only would make scratch gestures timid (no fast flicks); ±2 doubles the ring cost only on the reverse side (24 s bound) which is affordable. Forward overspeed is free (debt shrinks; clamped at the live head).
**Tradeoff:** 26 s ring (9–40 MB by fs). Accepted; documented.

---

## Special Considerations

### Thread Safety
- All parameter reads: `getRawParameterValue()->load()` atomics; cached raw pointers resolved once in the constructor (suite convention)
- ScratchLut: double-buffer + `std::atomic<ScratchLut*>`; message thread only ever writes the buffer NOT currently published; audio thread latches at engage edge
- UI readback: `std::atomic<float>` pass-phase + state enum as `std::atomic<int>`; editor timer polls, emits only when visible

### Performance
- Voice read (Catmull-Rom, 2 ch): ~2 % single core; two voices only for 50–300 ms windows
- Transport: one `pow` per sample worst case (~1 %)
- toneTrack: one tan per 16 samples — negligible
- Total estimate: < 5 % single core @ 48 kHz. No oversampling, no FFT.

### Denormal Protection
- `juce::ScopedNoDenormals` in processBlock; TPT filter state snapped to zero via `snapToZero` when idle; the stopped-state fade hits exact 0.0f (no decaying tails)

### Sample Rate Handling
- Ring reallocated in `prepareToPlay` (26 s at the new fs); all durations converted at gesture edges from ms/beats using current fs; no cached sample counts survive a rate change (transport reset in prepareToPlay)
- `prepareToPlay` also resets: voices, transport → Bypassed, filter, smoothers. Engage held ON across a transport reset re-triggers cleanly on the next edge evaluation (treat restored ENGAGE=on at prepare as an edge)

### Latency
- Zero. No `setLatencySamples` call needed (JUCE 8: `getLatencySamples()` is non-virtual — irrelevant here, nothing to report).

## Research References

### Professional Plugins
1. **Kilohearts Tape Stop** (free) — the parameter-set blueprint: Stop Time, Start Time, single Curve knob for motor speed shape. O-Tapestop's stop/start/curve trio matches this proven UX, adds per-direction curves + sync. ([kilohearts.com](https://kilohearts.com/products/tape_stop), [KVR](https://www.kvraudio.com/product/tape-stop-by-kilohearts))
2. **Cableguys TimeShaper** — drawable time-curve workflow; virtual playhead offset vs host timeline, "upward ramps speed playback, downward slow it; slower than realtime goes into reverse" — validates the bipolar drawn-envelope model and the offset-integral framing. ([Path C research doc](../../../..//research/stutter-effects/path-c-playhead-modulator.md))
3. **Image-Line Gross Beat** — 2-bar rolling buffer + 36 user time/volume envelopes; validates rolling-ring + drawn-envelope architecture at scale. ([adorama listing](https://www.adorama.com/ilgrossbeat.html))
4. **dBlue Glitch / Illformed Glitch 2** — tapestop as a gesture slot; simplicity of the engage-style trigger. (research/glitch-effects/README.md)
5. **Signalsmith (KVR t=538470)** — tape-start fall-behind → accelerate → crossfade-skip resync technique; the DSP-03 contract.
